title: Beginning in Bend
body:
Been a month since leaving White Salmon, WA to set out on this adventure. Still calling Washington home for now, but really the road is going to be home this spring and summer (though Alaska is always my real home, and our eventual destination this summer). 

The Alaskan winters finally got me to leave in 2022 to try something a little warmer in the region, close to fam and friends. After a stint in Portland, two stints in White Salmon (an unforgettable adventure or two on of their own), it's time to embark on an epic roadtrip with Wojo (the star and voice of this journal hereafter).

We'll be exploring the southwest, playing it by ear, and trying to save money to eventually land somewhere more permanent. We'll log our travels and experiences here as often as we can, but not too much. Next stop will be back up in The Gorge to take care of some business and see fam before really heading out.

The site and our voices will evolve over time. Please reach out directly if you know me or via the anonymous form in the Wandering Wojo panel on the main page here. 

Wish us luck! Hit us up! Send suggestions, essential albums, or whatever else you think might enhance the experience. We're excited, a little nervous, but really ready to have the roadtrip of a lifetime!

title: Touching Base
body:
Started feeling a bit antsy in Central Oregon… Ready to get on the road but taking care of odds and ends, errands, paperwork, setting up the truck, all while he’s working full time and we’re hopping from place to place, crashing guest rooms.. odd how this can feel claustrophobic. 

Felt amazing to get on the road, even if just on a trip back north to The Gorge. Just a tiny taste of what’s to come. Half-way through the ride I got a little restless, stuck in this mesh backpack the big guy got me. He let me out and holy shit… sounds, trees and lights moving faster than I ever realized they could. He let me sit on his lap towards the end of the ride while he sang with the big sounds, “You’ve got a friend… ‘aint it good to know…”

Now it’s just biding time in the hot room upstairs while it rains outside. I trust he’ll get our space all fixed up for the next leg of the ride. Meanwhile, I think I can see that he’s got some big feelings, maybe some sadness being back where he had his biggest dreams and almost made it all come together, but not quite.

I can see his eyes get watery sometimes, but I know he’s been through tough times and can handle this. He says his shoulder tat is about flexibility, agility, resilience… “Whatever way you throw him, he lands upright”. Anyway… kinda like me, I guess. Being a cat and all.

Still, I can hear him laughing and chatting with the fam he has here and knows it puts him at ease, maybe reminding him that it’s not just me who cares and looks after him. Seems like he loves them as much as I love him. Ugh, what a swirl of feelings. Let’s hope he finds some ease and smiles… maybe recharges a bit so we can start this adventure on the right paw.

title: The Precipice
body:
The adventure really begins tomorrow morning. It's been nice staying with family in The Gorge, buttoning up odds and ends, getting some laughs and hugs in. Even got to visit Black Cat one more time before she embarks on her final journey. What an opportunity to practice optimism and letting go (of everything, wonderful and sad alike). 

Sounds like we'll be staying in a campground with power, showers and even a restaurant, in Northern California for the first week. A nice opportunity to get a feel for our setup and what might be missing. 

It's been nice staying in the biggest house I've ever seen, with my own extra-warm room upstairs. I'm a bit anxious about being outdoors, but I dunno... I've acclimated to new spaces before and this might turn out to be not so bad. At least there will be a ton of new smells. 

Anyway, just touching base and getting this pin on the map before we move along. I sure love the people here, friends and family alike. Maybe I'll get to see them again soon.

title: Day 1... Woah, Jo...
body:
Welll... we landed. First real roadtripping day in the books. I hated the car ride. Flat out. I barked, yelped, moaned, until I found a nook in the back seat I could smash my face into and just close my eyes until it was over. I peed in my carrier... just seconds after I was in my litterbox. I don't know... I was frazzled... it was loud. I felt bad, but I cried wolf too many times and the big guy couldn't tell I really meant it when I finally had to go. 

We're in the tent now, listening to a stream and the occasional train pass by. The big guy grabbed dinner in this cute train car restaurant at the place we're staying and said he loved it... hippies playing sax jazz and guitar bossa nova... Ultra burger and a beer to wrap up the long day of driving. I guess he deserved it after putting up with the piss fest... even if he did make me wait in the car this morning while he visited and said he "felt great... god damn... what a trip... love love, happy hug blah blah." Humans... 

Anyway, he'll be back to work tomorrow morning, and we'll find our rhythm on the road. I'm beat... need some sleep. More journaling to come as we hang here a week.... I'm so tired I'm rhyming... a rhyming cat... anyway, gnight world.

Morning Update: I slept like a rock up in that tent... I think we both did. Still having a rough time with the sounds this moving house makes sometimes... but I ate some food and I'm starting to get curious about the world. I dunno, maybe this won't be half bad...

title: OOoookay
body:
Oooookay... today wasn't so bad. The big guy took pics of me to share, but there were plenty that weren't captured. I got to stretch my legs, sunbathe, scratch trees, eat grass, watch birds... And then a nice long nap in the truck. 

The decompression seems to finally be starting to hit... what now? There's no one. Actually, that's not true, Big guy's bestie happened to stop by for a quick visit. That was truly special and unexpected (see the cheesy pic of them hamming it up, eh they're alright).  

He also has some bright squares that his people seem to talk through with him. They show up from time to time to cheer him on, and me too it seems. The fun one with the food hair even spent some square time with him today... I can tell how much that puts him at ease and tugs on strings. Sounds like others even send messages through our journal, without even including their names... Anonymous encouragement feels so real. Thanks everyone 🫂

But... how the hell did I end up homeless with a 40 year old human in tow...? He says he's house hunting... But how to hunt when you don't even know where, or what for? Land to build? House to buy? Why? Why not? Maybe he needs to think more like a cat... we know how to hunt... 

Anyway, too many questions... the decompression seems to have paused. Think it's time to clean and get cozy for the evening. Maybe close my eyes and just feel grateful until I crap out. So damn deeply grateful.... 💤

title: Morning Time Now
body:
It's morning time now. lLstening to all of the sounds out here... chainsaws, a nearby river, birds, people... It's nice but still a lot to take in. So, yeah, I'm sitting on the big guy's lap, resting my chin on his arm, patiently waiting for the sun to come around and warm us up. Crazy how it can be so cold at night here, and so hot during the day!

Love seeing all the nice anonymous messages come in from our journal page! What a treat to be so loved...

title: Finding Ease
body:
Spent most of the day outside on the longer leash the big guy got me. Actually went for a little stroll with him and I gotta admit... once I got past the fear of the big sounds... I kind liked it. Lots of grass to chew, smells to sniff, bugs to chase. Not too shabby... No shab at all really.

Honestly, not much to report today besides finding a bit of space, relaxation, ease. Sometimes it's not about a flashy day, or grandiose things. Seems like sometimes the most grandiose is when we get to breathe, or at least remember that it's possible to breathe. 

How cool to be this fortunate... to just have trees show up... sunlight... hugs, kind and considerate messages of support and admiration, collaboration with good people. Screw the news... I choose this.

title: Planning...
body:
What a lazy day... but that's what cats crave. Still... Been thinking about the next destination. 

While doing a little research, its starting to feel a bit like Truman when he planned to go to Fiji... gas prices are suddenly exploding, a multi-week heat wave exactly where we're going... potential crash pads suddenly not responding... kinda like "fire at the plant!", a broken down bus... a freak localized storm directly over head...

Hmmmm... OK so it'll be unbearably hot and expensive in the Southwest... So we'll follow the temps and roam around here. Find some hot springs, visit the coast, pop into the mountains... hell we could go to Nebraska. Right?

Anyway, feels nice to let go and let it all happen. No need to get angry when the red dot you caught isn't really under your paw, but is actually back on the wall... Let's just enjoy the chase.

title: Family in Nevada
body:
Well... what an amazing Saturday we had... On a whim we blasted out of Shasta and down into the super warm valley below. Stunning green rolling hills, lush with plants and smells for feline nasal delight!! 

After rolling through that humid warmth we began back up the mountains through trees and into desert and snow to see some of the big guy's family tribe. 

They didn't see it, but I saw him get glassy eyes as he felt grateful for the incredible hospitality as they fed him and shared stories. We even got to sleep in a bed and meet two weird looking cats that were so excited and super sweet. 

Anyway, just a quick stop on our way south. More to come this evening. What an amazing whirlwind... amazing food for the soul. Can't wait to come back and hang a bit more :) 

"Shower the people you love with love."

title: Straddled
body:
We drove out of Reno and up through the Sierra Mountains, behind Yosemite, to keep a bit more cool today. A stunning drive that I savagely meowed through in its entirety. 

Now we're on the edge of the heatwave just south of us, straddled by the Sequoia National Forest to the west and Death Valley to the east. Its stunningly beautiful here, and honestly, the whole campsite has ground that's like natural kitty litter... maybe I'll experiment with that a bit in the next few days.

The plan is to hang tight and let the big guy work before mobbing out through the Mojave Desert to Flagstaff where it's higher and cooler, and then Grand Canyon Thursday evening. We'll do some off-grid camping and canyon exploring for a while after that.

Or at least that's what we're thinking. That can always change :)

On another note... What is meaning? Why the compulsion for closeness, comfort, familiarity? It's fascinating to observe oneself once all routine and regularity is removed. Knee-jerk reactions, creature comforts, annoyances, pleasant surprises. They just show up... And then decisions are made and then more things show up. What a stream. But what do I know? Why so contemplative? I'm just a friggin cat... I do notice that I'm getting more comfortable in the truck though, sitting on the console touching my nose to the big guy's arm. And with those weird big loud short faced "cats" at some people's houses... I guess they're not so bad. And all these new places and smells... I even got to stick my teeny nose tip out the window today to smell the passing mountain air.... Not too shabby... no shab at all. 

The balance of the familiar with the fresh is a fascinating back and forth... a dancing knife's edge I guess.. or cat's claw? Tooth? Poop?

title: Haht T'day
body:
We gaht haht t'day. Had to make plenty of use of that cold air inside the truck... And plenty of lazy laying around in the shade, with the breeze. Holy cow. 

But, the big guy had to do his screen work and it was otherwise low key. He painted our journal's web address on the tent for others to see. Not sure why tbh... But, why not? Who knows what random connections come of it 🤷‍♂️

Been thinking about that feeling of being rushed a lot. Seems like a lot of it has to do with whatever is going on outside (heat, cold, loud, the pressures of AI making everyone obsolete and the impetus it puts on people to do MORE, FASTER, NOW or face financial ruin)... But also how the inside is ordered (or not).

Anyway that rushed feeling sucks. Enjoying a fresh breeze, a bird, clean cool water, someone showing you how much you mean to them, the smell of spring wildflowers, shelter when it's needed, and freedom otherwise.

But so many of those pleasantries are bought with funds. Funds that may go away.... Seems like a tribe of great people are the way through that... trading, supporting, loving. And here we are, the big guy and I, far from that loving tribe, cooking in the desert. Maybe we have to fling ourselves far out away from our loves in order to someday offer them more, if we're lucky enough to find them again. Or maybe to break patterns, learn more... I dunno.

Or maybe we're just here, doing this, and that's ok. Come what may.

title: Death Valley Tomorrow
body:
Today was a chill as they come. Warm but not too hot. The big guy really tested out the solar/starlink setup and its not too shabby (i.e. no shab). He also jury-rigged some cardboard flaps under the tent to keep it from buzzing and flopping on the drive. Crossing our fingers on that one...

SO, the plan was to mob out 8 hours tomorrow after work, straight to Flagstaff. Screw that. I think the big guy took pity on me (and his stinky ass feet) and booked us a one night stay in Vegas. That cuts each leg into 4 hours. Then, we'll be overland off-grid camping for three nights near the entrance to the Grand Canyon! Maybe finally this big oaf will get me out on some hikes in my cat backpack!

So that's settled. He also had a great call with his boss today, talking through some deep/pressing things at work. The big guy really seems to feel rushed, pressured, worried, stressed, about staying relevant and useful. I can see it robbing him of his ability to enjoy things. This trip is so special and unique... he better figure it out before it's all behind him and he's rushed through it. 

Anyway I'm here cleaning myself in the cool tent while the big guy takes this down for me. I hope you all are digging the new "Your 2 cents" menu in the journal here... The polls, Same ability to message us and now the ability to help support us with gas/treat money. You can even direct how the big guy spends those funds in your donation message! GET ME SOME FISH! He'll take pics and make sure to post them in the next day's story for you :) 

Anyway, hug someone if you can. Talk to cool strangers if they're around (big guy met someone from his home town today!). Revisit past connections that you may have been hasty about (they may surprise you)...

People and our connections with them are all that matter it seems. And loving, charitable, curious fun connections (not the shit stabbing ass ripping kind). 

I love you guys and I think the big dude does also. Hit us up in the new menu!

title: Las Vegas
body:
The big guy thought he'd be clever and drive in the evenings after work. He thought he'd even push through Death Valley, thinking it wouldn't be too bad. 

I melted like furry butter... 108 degrees and no AC for much of it to keep the engine cooled off. That kinda heat is no joke it seems... 

Anyway, it was nice but also a little sad to say goodbye to the site we were at in Lone Pine, but I can't say I'll miss the dust... sheesh. 

Not a long journal entry tonight. We're just stopping over on our way to the Grand Canyon. Seems like there are some really nice people, and really cool hikes near here though. Might be worth swinging back through... 

The big guy was goofy excited and wanted to get a bunch of pics with me in Death Valley... He's gonna post them here but, just know (if you can't tell form the photos) that I wasn't feeling it. 

I'll touch base with yawls tomorrow. 

Oh PS... The big guy just mentioned that we're in the birthplace of my namesake, Wowajahowitz, the cat he grew up with, born the same year as him. I guess he named me after him because I look just like the elder Woj. Pretty cool. Whatever.

title: Diné Today
body:
5 years ago today, the big guy's step dad passed. He was an amazing guy, with a wild story, and a huge heart. Five years ago the big guy couldn't be there in person as Nakaii passed, but he dug a grave for him for when his ashes came back home to Resurrection Bay. 

Today the big guy's fam is back home in Alaska and we're out here in the middle of nowhere just south of the Grand Canyon's South entrance. 

From what Grandma says Nakaii was the coyote, but also came to people in dreams as a white horse or riding a white horse...

 Tonight, after the big dude gets all set up in his tent, I hear footsteps nearby and then he shouts out "hello?? Someone out there?"

He unzips his tent flaps and shines a light but it just lights up the screen... can't see anything. So as the footsteps continue he unzips the main tent door flap and sees a moonlit white horse walking off into the dark. 

There was one time Nakaii did the big dude an incredibly huge favor and said "You're Diné today." he'll forever be grateful. 

Tonight we sleep with the coyotes and horses, and the sound of people yelling at them in the distance. We remember and love Nakaii.
